title: Fugaro runs show
description: The document `fugaro runs show --json` prints: one run, the chain it belongs to and what is left of the chain's limits (docs/run-limit-carry-over spec §7, D1055, D1056). A chain is the unit of work whose runs share one limit (D1045): `chain` is the run that began it — not the run being shown — `run_count` is how many runs the link reached, and each `limits[]` row is one dimension the chain's own limit bounds, with what the chain has used of it and what is left. The limit is the figure the root launch was given (D1041) and is read out of that run's stored task; what has been used is read off the chain's runs — the dollars and tokens from the budget database's per-run ledgers, the wall time and review rounds from the run records (D1046, D1047). With the installation's budget off there is no ledger, the records are the figures, `enforced` is false — the spec's UNENFORCED — and the token dimension is reported unmeasured rather than approximated: `used` and `remaining` are null there, because no run record carries a whole-run token total (D1046, D1051). Members are only ever added within a version, so a renamed or re-meant member is a new member under a new name and the old one is kept, and removing or retyping one bumps version. No object here is closed for that reason: additionalProperties is left true everywhere, because a consumer that refused a member this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's document. The launch reply's `chain` and `limits[]` (D1056) are this same block, so the two cannot drift.

repo.description: The repository's own name (`acme/app`) of the run shown, the same value a row of runs ls carries and the launch reply reports.

run.description: The run shown, as `<storage-slug>/<run-id>` — the same form a row of runs ls carries and the launch reply reports, so a consumer reads the repository's storage key (the bucket prefix its objects live under) and the run id in one member. The `chain` member beside it is a bare run id: a chain is one repository's runs, and this is that repository.

chain.description: The run that began the chain (D1045): the run a pull request's branch is named for, the run a retry's stored task carries, or the run the chain was continued from. Empty is the one read that stopped at a gap — the chain's records name a link the bucket no longer holds anything under, so the run that began it was never read and rooting the chain at the oldest run that was read would name a run no link said was the root (runstore.Chain.Root). `run_count` then holds the runs the link still reached.
chain.$comment: Empty, never absent: the member is required, so a consumer branches on the value.

run_count.description: How many runs of the chain the link reached, the run shown among them. 1 is the ordinary shape of a first run, and 0 is a chain whose records could not be read at all.

enforced.description: Whether the money and token figures are the budget database's. False is the spec's UNENFORCED: the installation's budget is off, so the records are the figures and the chain is a report and not a stop (D1046, T10). A consumer that needs a stop must read this beside the figures.

limits_read.description: Whether the chain's limit was read at all. The figure lives in the stored task of the run that began the chain, and the bucket ages a run's objects out, so a chain whose root is older than that window has no limit left to read. True with an empty `limits` is a chain that bounds none of the four dimensions; false is a chain whose limit is unknown, and it is the only member that tells the two apart: a consumer that read an empty array alone would read a spent chain as a free one, which is what the null of an unmeasured dimension prevents one level down (D1051).

limits.description: One row per dimension the chain's own limit bounds, in the order every message about them reads: usd, tokens, time, review_rounds. A dimension the chain sets no figure for is absent rather than present at zero — nothing bounds it — and an empty array under a true `limits_read` is a chain that bounds none of the four. Empty under a false `limits_read` is a chain whose limit could not be read: its root run's stored task is gone, or the read stopped at a gap in the chain (an empty `chain`).

messages.$comment: Absent, never null, for a run whose record carries no messages block: a run that reads no messages has the block with accepting false, and a run from before the channel existed has none at all (internal/cli.messagesOf).

dimension.description: The dimension the row is about (runstore.Dimension), and the unit its three amounts are in: usd is micro-dollars (the unit the budget database's ledger, a limit and every other document count money in — runs summary's spent_micros), tokens is whole tokens, time is seconds, and review_rounds is a count. The amounts are the engine's own figures, unconverted, because the launch reply carries this same block and a conversion in one document and not the other is the drift the shared shape prevents.

limit.description: The chain's own limit in this dimension: the figure the run that began the chain was launched with (D1041), in the dimension's own unit. Never null: a row exists only for a dimension the chain bounds.

used.$comment: oneOf rather than a nullable number so that the two branches are named: null is the unmeasured dimension of D1051, not a zero.
used.description: What the chain's runs have already spent in this dimension (D1047), in the dimension's own unit: the dollars and tokens summed over the runs' budget ledgers (reserved less released, and the ledger's token leaf), the wall time off the records as max(elapsed, the sum of the stages' durations), and the review rounds as the count of the chain's reviews[] entries. Null is a dimension the chain does not measure — the token dimension of a chain whose budget is off, where no run record carries a whole-run token total (D1046, D1051) — and never a zero that was read.

remaining.description: What is left of the limit over what the chain has used: limit − used, in the dimension's own unit. It is not clamped at zero — a chain that spent past its limit reads as a negative, which is a chain that has spent and not an unspent one — and it is null exactly when `used` is, for the dimension the chain does not measure.

source.description: The policy layer the figure came from: `chain`, the chain layer's own name (policy.SourceChain, F4, D1055). A chain's limit is the root launch's own figure — the `--max-*` flags the launch that began the chain was given, merged as the chain layer (D1041, D1043) — and the limit is not read from any run record, so this member is not read from one either: a record's own sources name the layer that set each merge key, and the dollar key is also the repository's per-run cap, which the repository's own file may set (`branch`). A chain limit labelled with that layer names a place the number did not come from, which is the failure F4 exists to prevent. Before the chain layer had a name of its own, every layer past the first two was called `branch`. Not an enum here: a layer name is a string, and a consumer that refused one this schema has never heard of would refuse a newer CLI's document.

reason.description: The closed vocabulary's name for why the run stopped (runstore.HaltReason), such as run_cap or token_cap.

scope.description: The scope the limit it met was set at (runstore.Halt.Scope).

at.description: When the run was halted, RFC 3339 in UTC.

detail.description: The runner's own sentence for the halt, redacted the way every string diagnose prints is. Absent when the record carries none.

halt.description: The halt of a halted run, absent for a run that was not halted. A halted run's first question is how much is left, which is what this document's own figures answer (D1055).

accepting.description: Whether the run was taking messages at all (runmsg.Record.Accepting). False is a run launched with the channel off — and a diagnosis reports it as a run that reads no messages rather than as one that was merely sent none, the two being different readings of an empty list (F9). Not a licence to send one: whether a message is still taken is the launcher's own decision, and this member is what the run recorded about itself.

format.description: The format version the run's message block was written in (runmsg.Format; 0 in the block a diagnosis synthesizes for a run whose record carries none). A consumer reads the version before the members below, so a newer format's block is not read under this one's rules.

flags.description: The flags the launch wrote for the run's channel, each a name of runmsg's closed vocabulary (`now`, `wrap_up`) — the directives that hold for every message of the run, such as a run told to wrap up after the message it reads. Absent when the record names none. Not an enum, for the reason `source` is not one: a consumer that refused a name this schema has never heard of would refuse a newer CLI's document.

messages.description: One row per message, in number order: what the run recorded about it. The list is the record's own, so a run whose record carries no block has an empty list under accepting false, and a number the record does not mention is absent here — a diagnosis is the reader that adds those rows, from the objects under the bucket's prefix (F18). Bounded by the channel's own cap (runmsg.MaxMessages), which a diagnosis reads a few rows past so that the 21st message is visible as one no run reads (F12).

The run's own account of its message channel (docs/run-messages, D2940, F13): whether it was reading messages and what it recorded about each one it saw. The record is written by the run, whose own agent can rewrite it, so every fate here is what the run recorded and not what happened — `fugaro diagnose` is the reader that cross-checks these rows against the message objects under the bucket's `tokens/<slug>/<run>/messages/` and prints a number the record never mentions as one the run never read (F18, F20). The members that say so — `object`, `text_expired`, `text`, `line`, `line_note` — are a diagnosis's: this document is read off the record alone, and never opens the bucket.

seq.description: The message's number, and the name it is stored under: the object is `<seq, four digits>.msg.json` under the run's own messages prefix.

state.description: The fate the run recorded for this number (runmsg.State): `delivered`, read by the coder stage in `stage`; `undelivered`, still unread when the run ended; `refused`, an object the run would not read; and `missing`, a number between two it delivered whose object was not there when it polled — which a later write can fill, so a diagnosis reads it as one the agent never saw. Absent when the record states no fate for the number, and on a row the record does not mention. Not an enum that closes the vocabulary of a newer format: a consumer reads `format` first.
state.$comment: Absent, never empty-string, so that a consumer branches on the member rather than on a value that could also be a name it does not know.

recorded.description: Whether the run's record mentions this number at all. True for every row of the record's own list, and false for a row a diagnosis added from the bucket's prefix: a message object written after the run's last poll — the runner's last is at finalize (F18) — is one the run never read, and this member is what tells that row from a run that read the message and recorded it.

sent_at.description: When the message was written, RFC 3339 in UTC, as the run recorded it. The object carries its own time, which a diagnosis does not print: the record is what this document is.

sent_by.description: The address of whoever sent it, as the run recorded it. Redacted the way every string a command prints is.

flags.description: The flags this one message carried, one of the names of the block's own `flags`. Absent when it carried none.

stage.description: The stage that read a delivered message (`implement`, `review`, `fix`), as the run recorded it. Absent for a message no stage read, and for one a record states no stage for.

delivered_at.description: When a stage read it, RFC 3339 in UTC, as the run recorded it. Absent for a message no stage read.

reason.description: The run's own sentence for the fate — why a message was refused, or why it was never carried — redacted the way every string a command prints is. Absent when the record carries none.

object.description: Whether the message object is under the run's own prefix in the bucket, which is the question a diagnosis asks and a `runs show` does not. True is an object a diagnosis could read the text out of; false is one the bucket never had or has aged out after its seven days (F11). Absent in this document: `runs show` reads the record alone and has no answer about the bucket, which is a different member from a false that was read.

text_expired.description: A diagnosis's own reading: the record says the run never carried this message and the object is no longer there, so the text is gone and there is nothing left to send again (F11). Absent, never false, elsewhere: only a diagnosis looked.

over_cap.description: A diagnosis's own reading of a number past the channel's cap (runmsg.MaxMessages): no run reads it, however it was written, so the row says so rather than quoting a text the run never saw (F12). Absent, never false, elsewhere.

text.description: The message's own text, read out of the object by a diagnosis and printed under the fate. Absent when nothing was read: no object, a row over the cap, or a fate that needs no text. This member is the reason a diagnosis reads the object — the record holds no text at all, so a text that came from under `runs/` is not this one (F19).

line.description: The command that sends the message again, built by a diagnosis out of the object's text, this machine's own name for the repository and the number of the open pull request the code host reports for the run's branch — `fugaro run [--pr N] --repo <owner/name> -- '<text>'`. Never built from anything under `runs/`: the run's own record names a pull request the run's agent could have written, which is what F19 exists to keep out of a line a person pastes. Absent when there is no text to send, and its number is absent when the host cannot be asked or reports no open pull request for the branch.

line_note.description: Why the `line` above carries no `--pr`, when it does not: the code host could not be asked, or it reports no open pull request on the run's branch (it answers with closed and merged ones too, and a message sent under one of those follows up a pull request that is over), or this machine's config names no repository for the run. Printed beside the line rather than left for the reader to wonder about (F19).

fate.description: One message as the run recorded it, plus whatever a diagnosis read back about it. The run's own members come from the record and are forgeable by the run's agent, which is why every one of them is labelled as the run's own account (F20); the diagnosis's members come from the bucket and the code host, which the run cannot write (F19).
